Projects

log-plat↗ on GitHub (opens in a new tab)

Go

A distributed log pipeline. Agents tail log files and send batches over gRPC to a collector, which publishes them to Kafka. An indexer moves records from Kafka into OpenSearch, and a small REST API serves search. Redis handles rate limiting and a search cache.

The goal was to never lose a log line, even when a service crashes mid-stream. Every hop is allowed to retry, so duplicates are expected. Each document’s ID comes from the line’s position in its source file, so a redelivered line overwrites itself instead of creating a copy. A separate checker reads the original file and confirms every line reached OpenSearch. Across 17 fault-injection scenarios, it found zero missing lines.

  • Go
  • gRPC
  • Kafka
  • OpenSearch
  • Redis
  • Docker
How it was tested

Each chaos scenario writes 60,000 lines at 3,000 lines/s, injects a fault four seconds in, heals it, and then runs the checker. All 17 passed with zero missing lines in three full runs, using the whole stack in Docker on one laptop.

Process kills
SIGKILL the collector, Kafka, the indexer, the agent, or OpenSearch.
Network faults
Toxiproxy cuts the links to the collector, Kafka, and OpenSearch, adds 800 ms of latency, resets connections, throttles Kafka to 50 KB/s, and blackholes OpenSearch.
Forced duplicates
Drop the collector’s acks, or kill the indexer after a write but before its offset commit. These fail unless OpenSearch absorbs the redundant writes.
Crash loops
Kill the collector and the indexer three times each, and kill every service in sequence.

On the same laptop, the default config indexes about 70,000 lines/s. The limit is the indexer’s poll, write, commit cycle, not the agents or the collector.
